content: pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: SEV3 - Streaming p99 latency breach for shared-gpu-pool in us-west-2. Alert triggered: p99 > 10s for 5m. Affected route: /v1/streaming/generate. Tenant(s) with high qps: tenant-9142. pagerduty-bot: Pager: maya, oncall runbook: streaming-latency. incidents-bot: Incident channel created automatically (this thread). maya: acked. I’m on it. maya: quick ask — is this hitting only streaming or batch too? jonah: checking metrics now. jonah: p95 from 200ms -> 1.1s; p99 from 3.8s -> 12.4s starting ~8123456700. streaming stall traces show long recv stalls on chunked responses. jonah: logs show lots of blkio wait and IO wait on hosts hosting shared-gpu-pool. dstat: high await on /dev/nvme1n1. jonah: I see repeated cgroup writeback events, kernel flusher spikes. suspect noisy tenant doing heavy writeback (checkpointing / large dataset paging). li: I can run tenant isolation steps. What’s current customer impact? amelia_cs: CS: a few mid-market customers reported slow completions and timeouts. No billing impact yet but user-facing timeouts at 15s for some calls. ravi: is evicting tenant-9142 safe? any stateful jobs? jonah: tenant 9142 has long-running upload jobs this morning according to s3 access logs, likely background model checkpoint. maya: follow on-call runbook: try throttling tenant IO via cgroup first, then evict if no improvement. li: I’ll apply io.weight tweak to the cgroup and restart the task agent for that container. ops-bot: Suggested command: `sudo cgset -r blkio.weight=100 /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenants/tenant-9142` (confirm path for our host). jonah: better: use control plane admin API to set tenant throttle to 20% of pool IO. command: ```bash curl -X POST "https://control-plane/api/v1/tenants/9142/throttle" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"io_percent":20}'``` maya: be careful — admin API will cause brief reconnects to worker agents. expected impact: ~5-10s disruption for long uploads. li: applying io.weight now on host gpu-hw-07. li: applied. monitoring... jonah: dashboards updating — p95 down to 310ms within 30s. p99 trending down from 12.4s -> 6.2s. maya: good sign. continue monitoring for 10m. ravi: do we want to migrate high-qps traffic off shared pool to dedicated fallback? maya: yes, start routing new streaming requests from premium customers to dedicated-fallback-1. ops-bot: runbook command to reroute: ```bash curl -X POST "https://proxy/api/v1/routes/migrate" -d '{"route":"/v1/streaming/generate","from":"shared-gpu-pool","to":"dedicated-fallback-1","filter":{"customer_tier":"premium"}}'``` jonah: starting migration for premium customers now. mari: (reaction :thumbsup:) — note: mari not in thread list — ignore. amelia_cs: notifying affected customers with status update — will say we’re mitigating noisy-tenant IO and moving premium traffic to fallback. maya: follow-up: We saw KV-cache evictions spike after migration because higher memory pressure on dedicated nodes; reducing batch size on dedicated-fallback-1 by 2 helps. jonah: changed batching config: `max_batch_tokens: 512 -> 256` for fallback model. impact: small - latency improved, throughput slightly lower. li: after io throttle, disk writeback returned to normal on gpu-hw-07. p99 stabilized ~800ms. maya: good. keep throttle in place for 30m, then evaluate if tenant needs eviction. ravi: tenant-9142 ops contact? does CS want to call them? amelia_cs: yes, we’ll contact tenant ops and request they pause heavy checkpoints for 1hr or move to off-peak. send symbolic mitigation note. incidents-bot: added note to incident timeline: "io throttle applied to tenant-9142; premium traffic migrated to dedicated-fallback-1; batching reduced on fallback". maya: preparing post-incident tasks: - write a runbook tweak to detect cgroup.writeback spikes and auto-throttle - add alert for sustained p99 > 5s with blkio await > 50ms - consider autoscale buffer for shared-gpu-pool. jonah: logs snippet around peak: ```text 2026-03-12T15:11:32Z host=gpu-hw-07 blkio: writeback 0.32s, await 98ms, io-ms: 1200 repeated 2026-03-12T15:11:34Z pid=4321 tenant=9142 upload checkpoint /tmp/checkpoint-20260312.tar.gz 2026-03-12T15:11:35Z streaming: chunk-send delay 12400ms``` li: will keep throttle for 45m then re-evaluate. maya: assigning follow-ups: (maya) own runbook updates, (jonah) telemetry thresholds, (li) eviction plan if throttle doesn't hold, (amelia_cs) customer comms. ravi: do we need to open a billing-safe mitigation to avoid customer QoS? maya: no immediate billing change; CS will reach out. amelia_cs: sent initial customer message, will post follow-up once stable. ops-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV4 after p99 stabilized. pagerduty-bot: incident acknowledgement cleared from on-call after handover. maya: closing this thread in 1h if metrics remain stable. li: noted. jonah: leaving final logs and mitigation commands in runbook wiki: https://wiki.internal/incident/runbooks/noisy-tenant-io (link). maya: thanks everyone. (reaction :tada:)
